1. Cut chicken into bite-sized cubes and pat dry.
2. Whisk yogurt with lemon juice, oil, and all spices to create a thick marinade.
3. Coat the chicken thoroughly and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
4. Thread the chicken onto skewers and grill over high heat or in a tandoor.

Recipe: Chicken Tikka

Steps (Part 2):
5. Baste with butter and cook until the edges are slightly charred and the meat is juicy.

Cuisine: South Asian
Subcuisine: Indo-British / Punjabi
Recipe: Chicken Tikka Masala

Description:
A world-famous dish consisting of roasted marinated chicken chunks (tikka) tossed in a rich, creamy, and vibrant tomato-based gravy.

Recipe: Chicken Tikka Masala

Ingredients:
- Prepared Chicken Tikka
- Tomato puree
- Heavy cream
- Onions
- Ginger-garlic paste
- Cumin powder
- Coriander powder
- Butter
- Fresh coriander

Recipe: Chicken Tikka Masala

Steps (Part 1):
1. Sauté finely chopped onions in butter until soft and golden.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste and spices, cooking until fragrant.
3. Pour in tomato puree and simmer until the sauce thickens and oil separates.
4. Stir in the heavy cream and pre-cooked chicken tikka pieces.

Recipe: Chicken Tikka Masala

Steps (Part 2):
5. Simmer for 5 minutes and garnish with fresh coriander before serving.

Cuisine: South Asian
Subcuisine: Punjabi
Recipe: Cholley (Chickpea Curry)

Description:
A spicy and tangy North Indian staple made of tender chickpeas cooked in a dark, flavorful onion-tomato gravy with a special spice blend.

Recipe: Cholley (Chickpea Curry)

Ingredients:
- Chickpeas (Kabuli Chana)
- Onions
- Tomatoes
- Tea bags (for color)
- Amchur (Dried mango powder)
- Anardana (Dried pomegranate seeds)
- Ginger-garlic paste
- Green chilies

Recipe: Cholley (Chickpea Curry)

Steps (Part 1):
1. Soak chickpeas overnight and pressure cook with tea bags and salt until tender.
2. Heat oil and sauté onions until deep brown.
3. Add ginger, garlic, and tomato puree; cook until the base is thick and dark.
4. Stir in the chickpeas along with the spice blend (Amchur, Anardana, Cumin).

Recipe: Cholley (Chickpea Curry)

Steps (Part 2):
5. Simmer until the gravy is thick and coats the chickpeas; serve with Bhatoora.

Cuisine: South Asian
Subcuisine: Indian Dessert
Recipe: Coconut Barfi

Description:
A dense, fudge-like sweet made from freshly grated coconut and condensed milk, flavored with cardamom and garnished with silver leaf or nuts.

Recipe: Coconut Barfi

Ingredients:
- Grated coconut
- Sweetened condensed milk
- Ghee
- Cardamom powder
- Pistachios
- Sugar

Recipe: Coconut Barfi

Steps (Part 1):
1. Sauté the grated coconut in a small amount of ghee until the moisture evaporates.
2. Add condensed milk and sugar; cook on low heat while stirring constantly.
3. Add cardamom powder once the mixture begins to thicken and leave the sides of the pan.
4. Spread the mixture onto a greased tray and level the surface.

Recipe: Coconut Barfi

Steps (Part 2):
5. Allow to cool completely before cutting into diamond or square shapes.

Cuisine: South Asian
Subcuisine: Punjabi
Recipe: Bhatoora (Fried Wheat Bread Balls)

Description:
A large, fluffy, deep-fried leavened bread made from refined flour, traditionally served as a companion to spicy Cholley.

Recipe: Bhatoora (Fried Wheat Bread Balls)

Ingredients:
- All-purpose flour (Maida)
- Yogurt
- Baking soda
- Semolina (Suji)
- Sugar
- Oil for deep frying

Recipe: Bhatoora (Fried Wheat Bread Balls)

Steps (Part 1):
1. Mix flour, yogurt, baking soda, and semolina to form a soft, smooth dough.
2. Knead well and let the dough rest in a warm place for at least 2 hours to ferment.
3. Divide into lemon-sized balls and roll into thick, oval-shaped discs.
4. Deep fry in very hot oil, pressing down gently until the bread puffs up like a balloon.

Recipe: Bhatoora (Fried Wheat Bread Balls)

Steps (Part 2):
5. Flip and fry until light golden on both sides; serve hot.

Cuisine: South Asian
Subcuisine: Coastal Indian
Recipe: Mango and Coconut Chutney (Am ki Chatni)

Description:
A tropical, sweet, and tangy relish made with ripe mangoes and fresh coconut, balanced with tempered spices.

metadata.name: Mango and Coconut Chutney (Am ki Chatni)

Recipe: Mango and Coconut Chutney (Am ki Chatni)

Ingredients:
- Ripe mango pulp
- Freshly grated coconut
- Green chilies
- Mustard seeds
- Curry leaves
- Jaggery
- Salt

metadata.name: Mango and Coconut Chutney (Am ki Chatni)

text:
Recipe: Mango and Coconut Chutney (Am ki Chatni)

Steps (Part 1):
1. Blend mango pulp and grated coconut with green chilies into a semi-smooth paste.
2. Transfer to a bowl and stir in a little jaggery or sugar if needed.
3. Heat oil in a small pan and add mustard seeds and curry leaves until they splutter.
4. Pour the hot tempering over the chutney and mix well.

metadata.name: Mango and Coconut Chutney (Am ki Chatni)

5. Serve chilled as a side for snacks or rice.

text:
Cuisine: South Asian
Subcuisine: Mughlai / North Indian
Recipe: Naan

Description:
A soft, leavened flatbread traditionally baked in a tandoor, known for its pillowy texture and charred bubbles.

Recipe: Naan

Ingredients:
- All-purpose flour
- Yeast
- Sugar
- Yogurt
- Milk
- Butter or Ghee
- Nigella seeds (optional)

Recipe: Naan

Steps (Part 1):
1. Activate yeast in warm milk with sugar.
2. Mix flour with salt, yogurt, and the yeast mixture to form a soft dough.
3. Knead until elastic and let rise for 1-2 hours until doubled in size.
4. Roll into tear-drop shapes and sprinkle with nigella seeds or garlic.

Recipe: Naan

Steps (Part 2):
5. Bake at high heat (or on a tawa) until puffed and charred; brush with butter.

Cuisine: South Asian
Subcuisine: North Indian
Recipe: Aloo Gobi (Potato and Cauliflower Curry)

Description:
A classic dry vegetarian curry consisting of potatoes and cauliflower florets sautéed with turmeric and aromatic Indian spices.

Recipe: Aloo Gobi (Potato and Cauliflower Curry)

Ingredients:
- Cauliflower florets
- Potatoes
- Onions
- Tomatoes
- Ginger-garlic paste
- Turmeric
- Cumin seeds
- Garam masala

Recipe: Aloo Gobi (Potato and Cauliflower Curry)

Steps (Part 1):
1. Sauté cumin seeds and onions until light golden.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste and turmeric, then stir in the cubed potatoes.
3. Add cauliflower florets and toss to coat with the spices.
4. Cover and cook on low heat, occasionally stirring, until vegetables are tender.

Recipe: Aloo Gobi (Potato and Cauliflower Curry)

5. Finish with garam masala and fresh coriander; serve dry.

Recipe: Salty (Namkin) Lassi

Description:
A cooling and digestive yogurt-based drink, whisked with chilled water and flavored with roasted cumin and black salt.

Recipe: Salty (Namkin) Lassi

Ingredients:
- Fresh yogurt
- Chilled water
- Roasted cumin powder
- Black salt (Kala Namak)
- Fresh mint leaves
- Ice cubes

Recipe: Salty (Namkin) Lassi

Steps (Part 1):
1. Whisk the yogurt in a large pitcher until smooth and creamy.
2. Slowly add chilled water while continuing to whisk (or blend) until frothy.
3. Stir in the roasted cumin powder and black salt.
4. Pour into tall glasses over ice cubes.

Recipe: Salty (Namkin) Lassi

Steps (Part 2):
5. Garnish with a sprig of fresh mint and a pinch of cumin powder.

Subcuisine: Awadhi / Persian
Recipe: Shirmal (Persian Saffron Flatbread)

Description:
A slightly sweet, saffron-infused naan made with milk and ghee, traditionally served with rich kormas and nihari.

Recipe: Shirmal (Persian Saffron Flatbread)

Ingredients:
- All-purpose flour
- Milk
- Ghee
- Sugar
- Saffron strands
- Kewra water
- Baking powder

Recipe: Shirmal (Persian Saffron Flatbread)

Steps (Part 1):
1. Warm the milk and soak saffron strands until the milk turns a deep yellow.
2. Mix flour, sugar, and baking powder, then rub in the ghee until it resembles breadcrumbs.
3. Knead into a soft dough using the saffron milk.
4. Let the dough rest for 1 hour, then roll into thick, round discs.

Recipe: Shirmal (Persian Saffron Flatbread)

Steps (Part 2):
5. Prick the surface with a fork and bake in a tandoor or oven until golden and aromatic.

Recipe: Tandoori Masala

Description:
A versatile and smoky spice mix specifically designed for marinating meats and vegetables intended for high-heat roasting.

Recipe: Tandoori Masala

Ingredients:
- Coriander seeds
- Cumin seeds
- Kashmiri red chilies
- Dried ginger
- Garlic powder
- Amchur
- Mace
- Nutmeg
- Cinnamon

Recipe: Tandoori Masala

Steps (Part 1):
1. Dry roast whole spices (coriander, cumin, chilies, cinnamon) on low heat until aromatic.
2. Allow the roasted spices to cool completely.
3. Grind into a fine powder using a spice grinder.
4. Mix in the powdered ingredients like ginger, garlic, and amchur.

Recipe: Tandoori Masala

Steps (Part 2):
5. Store in an airtight glass jar away from direct sunlight.

Recipe: Traditional Pilau Rice

Description:
A fragrant rice dish where Basmati grains are sautéed with whole spices and cooked in a seasoned broth for maximum flavor absorption.

Recipe: Traditional Pilau Rice

Ingredients:
- Basmati rice
- Onions
- Whole spices (Cardamom, Cloves, Bay leaf)
- Ghee
- Vegetable or Meat stock
- Saffron

Recipe: Traditional Pilau Rice

Steps (Part 1):
1. Soak Basmati rice for 30 minutes and drain.
2. Heat ghee and fry sliced onions until golden brown, then add whole spices.
3. Stir in the rice and sauté gently for 2 minutes to coat the grains in fat.
4. Add the stock (double the volume of rice) and salt.

Recipe: Traditional Pilau Rice

Steps (Part 2):
5. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on the lowest heat (Dum) until the liquid is absorbed.

Recipe: Chukauni (Nepalese Potato Salad)

Description:
A specialty from Western Nepal, this is a tangy potato and yogurt salad tempered with mustard oil and turmeric.

Recipe: Chukauni (Nepalese Potato Salad)

Ingredients:
- Boiled potatoes
- Thick yogurt
- Onions
- Green chilies
- Mustard oil
- Fenugreek seeds
- Turmeric powder

Recipe: Chukauni (Nepalese Potato Salad)

Steps (Part 1):
1. Cube the boiled potatoes and mix them in a bowl with yogurt, sliced onions, and green chilies.
2. In a small pan, heat mustard oil until it begins to smoke.
3. Add fenugreek seeds; once they turn dark brown, add turmeric powder.
4. Immediately pour the hot tempered oil over the potato-yogurt mixture.

Recipe: Chukauni (Nepalese Potato Salad)

Steps (Part 2):
5. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve cold as a side dish.

Recipe: Jhilinga (Nepalese Rice Fritters)

Description:
Delicate, colorful, and crunchy ring-shaped crackers made from rice flour, commonly prepared during the Tihar festival.

Recipe: Jhilinga (Nepalese Rice Fritters)

Ingredients:
- Rice flour
- Water
- Food coloring (optional)
- Oil for deep frying

Recipe: Jhilinga (Nepalese Rice Fritters)

Steps (Part 1):
1. Cook rice flour with water to create a thick, dough-like paste.
2. Pass the hot paste through a traditional mold (extrude) to form thin, circular noodle-like shapes.
3. Dry the circular shapes in the sun for 1-2 days until they are completely hard and brittle.
4. Deep fry the dried rings in hot oil; they will expand and become white or colorful.

Recipe: Jhilinga (Nepalese Rice Fritters)

Steps (Part 2):
5. Serve as a crunchy snack or as part of a ceremonial meal.

Recipe: Tibetan Meat Momos

Description:
Classic Himalayan dumplings stuffed with juicy minced meat and scallions, served with a fiery 'Momo Achar' (tomato chutney).

Recipe: Tibetan Meat Momos

Ingredients:
- All-purpose flour
- Minced beef or lamb
- Onions
- Ginger-garlic paste
- Soy sauce
- Scallions
- Sichuan pepper (Timmur)

Recipe: Tibetan Meat Momos

Steps (Part 1):
1. Knead a simple dough of flour and water; let it rest for 30 minutes.
2. Mix minced meat with onions, scallions, ginger-garlic, soy sauce, and a pinch of Sichuan pepper.
3. Roll the dough into small, thin circles.
4. Place a spoonful of filling in the center and pleat the edges to seal into a half-moon or round shape.

Recipe: Tibetan Meat Momos

Steps (Part 2):
5. Steam in a tiered steamer for 10-12 minutes and serve hot.

Recipe: Butter Tea (Po Cha)

Description:
An essential Himalayan beverage made from tea leaves, yak butter, and salt, providing warmth and calories in high-altitude climates.

Recipe: Butter Tea (Po Cha)

Ingredients:
- Black tea (Pu-erh style)
- Water
- Yak butter (or cow butter)
- Salt
- Milk

Recipe: Butter Tea (Po Cha)

Steps (Part 1):
1. Boil tea leaves in water for a long period until the decoction is very dark.
2. Strain the tea into a traditional wooden churn (or a modern blender).
3. Add salt, milk, and a generous amount of butter.
4. Churn or blend vigorously for 2-3 minutes until the tea is completely emulsified and creamy.

Recipe: Butter Tea (Po Cha)

Steps (Part 2):
5. Serve hot in small bowls or cups.
